name: Russian
review: Russian as written in Ukraine (the maintainer's ruling, 2026-11-19). Usage notes written in Russian that day by a writer briefed as an editor living in Ukraine, told nothing of cron, who found no difference in the language of schedules between Ukraine and the Russian Federation (carriers' own Russian texts could not be found; several reference works are cited from memory). Answers, lexicon and hand-written rows by Claude Fable 5.2 the same day, without reading the Ukrainian artifacts: three author passes against one adversarial schedule read of all 634 rows and two blind readers briefed as editors in Ukraine, asked for every reading of each sentence. Renderer built by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row: 152 of 153 held-out rows on the first judged run (the miss and two hard cases settled against the rows). Audited by an independent agent: two wrong schedules repaired test-first (29 February said as yearly; a fifth weekday said without its condition) and several unholdable forms. Not read by anyone independent: the 124 forms of the last author pass and the 46 the audit changed. Thin evidence: «в чётные часы» (two blind readers, no corpus source; Russian's ordinal count of hours is a known risk); ordinal minutes; «по будням» (usage notes and three Ukrainian Russian-language pages). Known heavy forms: eight or nine windows for minutes under scattered hours. Taste calls by the orchestrating model (Claude Fable 5.2) are recorded in the answers with their evidence; 2026-11-19, the reading check: all 674 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in Russian (4,786 questions about moments, 99.9% of answers right against an answer key that shares no code with the library); the 3 questions most readers got wrong were asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers, and none was still misread by most readers of both, so nothing was changed. Noted, one model only: «в последний день каждого месяца в 0:00» at 30 November (two of three Sonnet readers alone); «каждую минуту с 9:00 до 9:29 и в 9:45» at 9:37 (one). 2026-11-19, after the cost pass: all the odd hours under one minute are said by parity («в начале каждого нечётного часа» for «каждые 2 часа с 1:00 до 23:00»), and a rhythm of minutes under more than four scattered hours names the hours once and then the step inside the hour («каждые 3 часа, каждые 15 минут с начала часа по 45-ю минуту» for eight windows), chosen over rejected candidates with two blind readers briefed only in Russian; the reading check then read all 686 rows (4,895 questions, three Sonnet 5.5 readers), the 3 questions most readers missed (none in the changed forms) were asked again alone of Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 readers, and none was still misread by most readers of both. 2026-11-20: hours that fill the day from midnight (`*/2`, `*/3`, `*/4`) are said by their step, or by parity, whatever the minutes («каждые 3 часа, на 30-й минуте часа» for «каждые 3 часа с 0:30 до 21:30»; «на 30-й минуте каждого чётного часа»); the 19 changed and neighbouring rows were read by three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers briefed only in Russian (342 questions, none misread). 2026-11-20: hours that stand apart are named once and the minutes said once for all («ежедневно в 1, 4, 9, 14 и 18 часов, на 5-й и 35-й минуте часа»), in place of ten clock times or five windows; readers of two models briefed only in Russian answered every question on the 43 changed rows correctly. Stable 2026-11-25: every row has passed the reading check in its current wording (docs/language-status.md).
